news.title: The Caspian Pipeline Consortium has been attacked again
news.description: The Caspian Pipeline Consortium (which connects Kazakhstan’s largest oil fields with the Black Sea coast near Novorossiysk) has lost one of its three single-point mooring systems — SPM-2 — as a result of an attack carried out by an unmanned boat.
news.longText: The Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) is facing a new problem: as a result of an attack by a Ukrainian unmanned boat, one of its three single-point mooring systems — SPM-2, located in the Black Sea — has been put out of operation. The incident may significantly affect Kazakhstan’s oil export volumes in 2026, since more than 80% of the country’s supplies pass through CPC infrastructure. According to Kommersant, a full replacement of the damaged equipment could cost up to $120 million and take a long time — possibly until the summer of next year — a prospect that is causing concern among market analysts. The attack on SPM-2 has become the third incident targeting the consortium’s facilities, following strikes on the Kropotkinskaya pumping station and the administrative office in Novorossiysk. The company clarified that no tankers were being loaded at the time of the strike, and the device’s hoses were empty, which helped prevent an environmental disaster. However, further operation of the damaged module is impossible, and the consortium now faces significant expenses for lifting and dismantling it. The situation is further complicated by the fact that another system, SPM-3, is currently undergoing scheduled maintenance, meaning that the load on the only functioning SPM-1 is increasing sharply. Under normal operating conditions, the consortium uses two mooring systems simultaneously, keeping the third in reserve to ensure reliability. Now, with one system destroyed and another under repair, CPC’s oil throughput plans are at risk. Experts believe that the consortium may be forced to urgently bring SPM-3 back into service, but even that would not guarantee stability: the systems are not designed for continuous, uninterrupted operation, and winter storms combined with the threat of new attacks may repeatedly halt shipments. Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs reacted very sharply to the incident, issuing a protest and describing the attack as an action that undermines bilateral relations with Ukraine. The Kazakh authorities demanded guarantees from Kyiv that similar incidents would not occur again and urgently initiated a plan to explore alternative routes for its oil. However, experts note that any alternative pathways — such as those through Azerbaijan and Turkey — would be significantly more expensive for Kazakhstan and the CPC shareholders, ultimately reducing the country’s budget revenues. Analysts predict that even under an optimistic scenario, oil exports through CPC will decline in December and during the first half of 2026. First, the need to complete repairs of the hoses on SPM-3 has not gone away. Second, frequent shutdowns of port operations due to drone-attack threats are disrupting tanker schedules. Moreover, the worsening security situation in the Black Sea — where ships under the Gambian flag were recently targeted — will inevitably increase freight and insurance costs, adding additional pressure on market participants.

news.title: Ali Kerimli, Leader of One of Azerbaijan’s Oldest Opposition Parties, Arrested
news.description: «Ali Kerimli, the leader of the Popular Front Party of Azerbaijan, has been arrested for two and a half months on charges of attempting a violent seizure of power, sparking widespread debate and concern among human rights groups.»
news.longText:
«Authorities in Azerbaijan have arrested Ali Kerimli, the leader of the Popular Front Party of Azerbaijan (PFPA), for two and a half months on charges of attempting a violent seizure of power. Several other key opposition figures were detained alongside the head of one of the country’s oldest opposition parties. Human rights groups say the country has been experiencing a wave of repression for the past two years, and the number of political prisoners is now the highest since the early 2000s.

Under the charge of attempting a violent takeover, Kerimli faces a prison sentence ranging from 12 years to life. He was detained on Saturday, and on Monday a court ordered his arrest for two months and 13 days.

Pro-government media claim that during a search, the State Security Service found letters allegedly written by Ramiz Mehdiyev — the former head of the presidential administration who had previously been accused by the same media outlets of plotting a coup. However, Mehdiyev’s status as an accused party has not been officially confirmed.

The PFPA has long faced political pressure, with its members jailed even before 2019, when Mehdiyev left his position in President Ilham Aliyev’s administration. Shortly before his arrest, Kerimli publicly denied any connection between his party and Mehdiyev.

The arrest sparked intense debate on social media, where many commenters expressed disbelief that Kerimli and an elderly former official would plot a coup together — and keep physical letters as evidence.»

news.title: The leader of the Azerbaijani community was detained in Yekaterinburg
news.description: The new leader of Azerbaijanis in the Urals, Vidadi Mustafayev, has been detained in Yekaterinburg. Preliminary reports indicate he is suspected of fraudulent activities related to land sales. Testimony against Mustafayev may have been provided by a former lawyer.
news.longText: Security forces in Yekaterinburg have detained Vidadi Mustafayev, head of the 'Center for Culture, Youth, and Sports of Azerbaijanis of the Urals.' According to 66.RU, the operation was carried out by OBOP officers with support from SOBR units. Mustafayev was detained as he was leaving the Iset Tower after a workout. The publication reports that Vidadi Mustafayev is suspected of fraudulent activities related to land sales. In early September, Mustafayev announced that he had taken leadership of the Azerbaijani community in the Urals: “In this position, I plan to work on educating the youth, as no one has explained to them what is right and wrong; we will explain that it is necessary to live according to the norms of Russian law.” Previously, the head of the Azerbaijani diaspora in the Urals was Shahin Shykhlinski, chairman of the “Azerbaijan-Urals” organization. There was a prolonged conflict between him and Mustafayev. Since early August, Shahin Shykhlinski has been in custody. He is accused of attempting to murder entrepreneur Fehruz Shirinov in 2010. Vidadi Mustafayev was also recently involved in a criminal case. He acted as an intermediary in the delivery of a bribe from the former mayor of Sredneuralsk, Andrey Zashlyapin, to an officer of the Sverdlovsk Regional FSB. Mustafayev was exempted from criminal liability because he reported the crime to law enforcement authorities.

news.title: Stalled in Florida: How the U.S.-Ukraine Peace Plan Talks Ended
news.description: The U.S.-Ukraine talks in Florida delivered what Washington feared most — no final decision. Key issues remain unresolved. Experts put it bluntly: they failed to sway Ukraine, and the peace plan is stalled.
news.longText: Two rounds of negotiations in Florida, big names in the room — Rubio, Whitcoff, Kushner, Umerov — and not a single concrete decision at the end. Military analyst Yuri Baranchik sums up the outcome in one sentence: they agreed on everything except the main issues. According to him, on secondary points such as the election calendar and the general framework of a future agreement, the parties made some progress. But the territorial question and Ukraine’s real status remain a minefield. Kyiv is still not ready to see Crimea and Donbas as part of Russia, the U.S. is unwilling to risk accusations of “abandoning an ally,” and Europe is introducing amendments that directly contradict the American proposals. One plan envisions halving the size of the Ukrainian Armed Forces, another removes any limits entirely. One promises a non-aligned status, another keeps the NATO option slightly open. Military expert from Volgograd Anton Shchepetnov sees the Florida talks as a predictable failure: “The Americans wanted to play a soft game — apply some pressure, make a few promises, and package Kyiv’s defeat in a diplomatic wrapper,” he says. “But Kyiv stuck to its slogans, as usual. For them, it’s not really about peace, it’s about the image that they didn’t give anything away.” According to Shchepetnov, Washington tried to sell Ukraine roughly the following: formally, you do not abandon NATO, but in practice, you won’t be admitted; on paper, you do not recognize territorial changes, but you accept the front line. “For Moscow, this is not an option. Russia has clearly stated — Crimea and Donbas must be recognized as ours, and Ukrainian troops must leave Donbas. Until this is in writing, this is not a peace plan, it’s a scenario for a talk show,” he adds. U.S. media note that a scenario was discussed in which Ukraine would de facto lose the path to NATO — security agreements would be concluded between Washington, NATO, and Moscow, with Kyiv merely informed of the outcome. On paper, it sounds elegant, but for the Ukrainian elite, it is political suicide. Kyiv’s negotiators again presented the usual set of red lines: no territorial concessions, no reduction in army size, NATO and EU must be part of the security guarantees. As a result, there are no guarantees, NATO remains at best a shadow, and hostilities continue. Marco Rubio, after the meeting, maintained an optimistic tone — speaking of productive sessions, long-term security, and Ukraine’s prosperity. But he also acknowledged that much work lies ahead, the “equation” cannot be solved without Russia, and final decisions will only come after Trump’s special envoy visits Moscow. Experts read between the lines — the U.S. is forced to rely on direct talks with Moscow because pushing conditions through Kyiv does not work. Blogger Yuri Podolyaka and war correspondent Alexander Kots summarize: on the main issues, there has been no breakthrough; the Americans, “sincerely wanting to end the war,” are blocked by Kyiv’s uncooperative regime. Shchepetnov believes that the Florida pause may even benefit Russia: “Any attempt to close the conflict at the expense of territories declared Russian, or our interests, will fail. Until the U.S. is ready to acknowledge what has already happened on the ground, what they will have on their table is not a peace treaty, but a set of nice wishes. Russia will only negotiate on what is recognized as reality on the front or will imminently become so.” The Florida talks revealed the main point — without considering Moscow’s position and honestly recognizing the new territories, all plans remain a paper architecture. And paper, as experience shows, does not withstand the heat of real military action and quickly turns to ashes.

news.title: Russia secretly sells huge tracts of land in the Far East to China in exchange for 'war loans' - sources in the Ministry for the Development of the Russian Far East
news.description: The Ministry for the Development of the Far East and the Arctic and a senior official at a major Russian bank told the publication about a secret deal between Moscow and Beijing
news.longText: Three independent sources in the Ministry for the Development of the Far East and the Arctic and one senior employee of a major Russian bank told the publication about a secret deal between Moscow and Beijing: the Russian Federation transfers to China for a long-term lease (actually for 99 years) more than 1,2 million hectares of land in the Primorsky, Khabarovsk Territories and the Amur Region in exchange for irrevocable financing of the war in Ukraine in the amount of at least $38 billion in 2025-2027. «These are no longer loans, this is a direct calculation of land,» says the first source from the Ministry for the Development of the Russian Far East. - Officially, everything is formalized as «investment projects of the PRC in agriculture and logistics», but in fact it is the sale of territory. The Chinese get land, forests, rivers, and even the right to build gated communities with their own jurisdiction.» The second source shows an internal document marked «Top Secret»: 1.        480 thousand hectares in Primorye under the «grain cluster» 2.        370 thousand hectares in the Khabarovsk Territory for a «logistics hub» 3.        380 thousand hectares in the Amur Region for «animal husbandry and processing» «For every billion dollars - about 30-35 thousand hectares. The price per hectare is symbolic - about $ 30 thousand, while the market price in those places is from $ 150 thousand,» the third source clarifies. A fourth source from the banking sector: «The money has already started to arrive. The first tranche of $8.4 billion came in October through a chain of offshore companies. These funds were directly used to pay for Iranian drones, North Korean shells and salaries for the mobilized. Everything is framed as «Chinese investment in joint projects».» Press service of the Ministry for the Development of the Russian Far East: «There are no transactions for the sale of land to foreign countries. Everything is ordinary investment agreements within the framework of intergovernmental agreements.» The Chinese Embassy in Moscow declined to comment. One of the sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity, added: «In 20-30 years, there will already be Chinese cities with Chinese schools and Chinese police. We are just selling the future for today's shells.» The information is based solely on the testimony of anonymous sources and closed documents that came into the possession of the editorial board.

news.title: The Kremlin officially confirmed: starting January 1, 2026, Russia will switch to a six-day workweek
news.description: Putin has signed the decree: Saturday becomes a full working day, 40-hour workweek, annual leave and retirement age remain unchanged. The reform will first apply to the defense industry, fuel and energy sector, and continuous-cycle plants; starting in 2027 — almost everyone.
news.longText: The press service of the President of the Russian Federation has issued an official statement: Vladimir Putin signed a decree introducing a six-day working week for most categories of employed citizens starting January 1, 2026. The document has already been published on the official legal information portal. The main goal of the reform, as stated in the explanatory note, is «to maintain high rates of industrial production and economic activity amid external sanctions pressure and the need for import substitution.» Key provisions of the decree: •        Working week: 6 days (Monday–Saturday), total duration: 40 hours •        Saturday is recognized as a full working day with single-rate pay •        Maximum working day duration: 8 hours (exceptions possible for certain industries under collective agreements) •        Annual paid leave remains at 28 calendar days •        Retirement age remains unchanged Presidential press secretary Dmitry Peskov emphasized that the transition will be gradual: in 2026, the six-day week will apply to continuous-cycle enterprises, defense industry, fuel and energy complex, and critical infrastructure. From 2027, the measure will extend to other sectors except the public sector and small businesses. «This is not a return to Soviet practices, but a forced measure to preserve the competitiveness of the economy. We see that a number of Asian countries successfully operate in this mode and demonstrate impressive growth,» Peskov told reporters. The Ministry of Labor has already begun preparing explanations for employers. Trade unions announced they will push for compensatory measures: higher coefficients for Saturday work for certain categories and additional days off once per quarter. Reactions among economists are mixed: some call the decision «tough but necessary,» while others predict increased social tension and growth of the shadow economy.

news.title: The Kremlin is purposefully destroying its population in the war: sources from the Ministry of Defense revealed a plan for «demographic cleansing»
news.description: Three anonymous high-ranking sources in the Ministry of Defense of the Russian Federation independently told the publication about the existence of a secret plan to deliberately reduce the population of Russia through massive losses in the war in Ukraine.
news.longText: Three anonymous high-ranking sources in the Ministry of Defense of the Russian Federation independently told the publication about the existence of a secret plan to deliberately reduce the population of Russia through massive losses in the war in Ukraine. «This is not a war for Donbass, this is a war against our own people, says the first source close to the General Staff. — In closed reports, everything is called «demographic optimization». Figures for losses are planned in advance: 50-70 thousand per month. The main goal is to get rid of «extra mouths»: the unemployed, residents of depressed regions, ethnic minorities. At one of the closed meetings, Putin allegedly said: «It is better to lose a million there than to feed two million here».» The second source from the mobilization department adds: «The orders from above are simple: do not pull out the seriously wounded, do not rotate, do not issue reservations to those who are «not sorry».» They specifically take Buryatia, Tuva, Dagestan, poor regions of the Volga region - there is a higher birth rate, and the social system is more expensive. In three years, they plan to «write off» 2-3 million men aged 25-45. This will automatically solve the problem of future pensions and a decrease in the birth rate.» A third source, a former analyst of one of the special services: «There are closed calculations: with losses of 1.5 million, budget savings will amount to about 5 trillion rubles in 15-20 years. Everything is framed as a «patriotic duty», but in fact it is the genocide of its own population at the hands of Ukrainians. Convenient: heroes, funeral notices, payments to families - and no questions asked.» Press service of the Ministry of Defense of the Russian Federation: «Complete nonsense and provocation of the enemy. All losses are exclusively from the actions of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.» The information is based solely on the testimony of anonymous sources and has no documentary evidence.

news.title: Ukraine Hits Russia's ‘Shadow Fleet’ Tankers in the Black Sea and a Terminal in Novorossiysk. Kazakhstan and Turkey Protest
news.description: Ukrainian sea drones struck two tankers from Russia’s ‘shadow fleet’ in the Black Sea, as Kazakhstan and Turkey issued protests following the attack on tankers and a terminal in Novorossiysk.
news.longText:
Ukrainian maritime drones hit two oil tankers belonging to Russia’s so-called ‘shadow fleet’ in the Black Sea, while reports also indicated a strike on the Caspian Pipeline Consortium terminal in Novorossiysk. According to Turkish authorities, the impacted vessels — *Kairos* and *Virat* — sail under the flag of Gambia and are listed under EU and UK sanctions for transporting Russian oil in violation of international restrictions.

BBC Verify confirmed the authenticity of footage showing the drones approaching and detonating near the ships. Turkey stated the attacks occurred within its exclusive economic zone. The Ministry of Transport reported that the *Virat* sustained minor damage to its starboard side but remained stable; no casualties were reported. Published footage also shows Turkish rescue boats attempting to extinguish a fire on the *Kairos*.

According to an unnamed Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) official, both tankers were empty and heading to the Russian terminal in Novorossiysk. The source said the Sea Baby drones disabled vessels that could have transported up to $70 million worth of oil, helping the Kremlin circumvent sanctions.

Kazakhstan lodged a formal protest regarding the strike on the Novorossiysk terminal.

Turkey strongly condemned the attacks, stressing that they posed a serious threat to navigation, human safety, property, and environmental security in the region. Russian authorities have not yet commented on the incident. The situation continues to develop.

news.title: In the Moscow region, a pensioner won a lawsuit against housing and communal services and now receives hot water around the clock for free until 2035
news.description: Galina Ivanovna Smirnova, a 78-year-old resident of house No 17 on Lenin Street in Khimki, won a lawsuit against the local MUP «Teploset» and is now officially exempt from paying for hot water for the next 10 years.
news.longText: According to employees of the Khimki City Court, it all started with the fact that the pensioner had been keeping a diary of the temperature of the water in the tap since 2018 and recorded every case when it was below 60 ° C. Over seven years, 2,847 records with photos and thermometer measurements have accumulated. «She came with three thick folders and said: «I'm not for money, I'm for justice»,» says a source in the court. The judge satisfied the claim in full: he recognized a systematic violation of the Sanitary Rules and Regulations and ordered «Teploset» not only to return all payments for the last three years (187 thousand rubles), but also to provide G.I. Smirnova with free hot water supply until December 31, 2035 «as compensation for moral damage and legal costs». The press service of the MUP «Teploset» said that «the decision will be appealed, but so far the hot water meter in the pensioner's apartment has been sealed, and there are already zero rubles in the receipts for December. Neighbors in the riser are already buying thermometers en masse and starting diaries. One of them, on condition of anonymity, admitted: «Galina Ivanovna is now a local legend. He says that if something happens, he will tell everyone how to measure correctly».

news.title: Exclusive: 'General Gerasimov survived hell in the barracks': shocking revelations of former colleagues
news.description: Three anonymous sources who claim to have served alongside the current Chief of the General Staff of the Russian Armed Forces, Valery Gerasimov, in the late 1970s in the Far Eastern Military District, independently told our publication the same story about the group sexual abuse of young Lieutenant Gerasimov by senior servicemen.
news.longText: It was in 1979, he had just graduated from school, thin, with glasses, so quiet, `recalls the first source, a former sergeant. `The `grandfathers` decided to `lower` him. After lights out, they dragged me into the dryer, three held me, two ... well, you get the idea. He didn't shout, only wheezed. Then for a week he walked like a shadow, he could hardly move his legs.` The second source (a retired officer, then a senior lieutenant) confirms the details: `Everyone knew, but kept silent. The company commander simply turned away - he said, `it's his own fault, he didn't know how to put himself.` After that, Gerasimov changed: he became cold, hard as ice. They say that it was then that he swore that this would not happen again in the army - and he hates any `hazing` to this day. A third source, now a civilian, adds: `He was also filmed. One of the `grandfathers` boasted that the cassette was still lying somewhere. Then he was quietly transferred to another unit so that there would be no scandal. But the scars remained - look at him at parades, you can see everything in his eyes.` The press service of the Ministry of Defense of the Russian Federation responded to the request succinctly: `This is a pure provocation and fake. In Soviet times, all such rumors were carefully checked and refuted. There are no facts.` Witnesses could not provide documents or photos - `everything was destroyed back then.` But one of them noted: `In the 1970s, hazing was everywhere, especially in the Far East. Cases of violence are common, officers turned a blind eye.` The information is based solely on the testimony of anonymous sources and has no official confirmation. We will continue to investigate. If you have additional details, write anonymously.

news.title: State Duma proposes expanded oversight of regional development funds
news.description: Lawmakers argue that additional monitoring tools could reduce risks of misuse of regional development funds.
news.longText: The State Duma’s budget committee has proposed strengthening federal oversight over regional development funds, citing “the need for greater transparency.” The initiative follows an internal audit that identified several instances of “uncoordinated spending” in select regions. Regional officials privately warn that the new rules could complicate access to financing and increase their administrative burden. Analysts say the proposal reflects growing tensions between the federal center and regional administrations amid a slowdown in economic activity.

news.title: Authorities in Zabaykalsky Krai investigate reports of supply disruptions in military unit
news.description: Local authorities launched an inquiry after servicemen complained about delays in food supplies.
news.longText: The administration of Zabaykalsky Krai has announced an internal review after a video circulated online in which servicemen from a local unit complained about delayed food deliveries. The regional Defence Ministry maintains that “some details in the video are distorted,” but confirmed that logistical difficulties had occurred in November due to harsh weather and strained transport routes. Sources familiar with the situation say that one of the contractors failed to meet the delivery schedule, prompting emergency redistribution of supplies between units.

news.title: Finance Ministry updates schedule for government bond placement after brief delay
news.description: Federal loan bonds remain one of Russia’s primary budget financing tools, and any shift in demand for them immediately affects the national economy.
news.longText: Federal loan bonds are government debt securities issued by the Ministry of Finance of Russia to borrow money from banks, corporations, and private investors. By purchasing these bonds, investors effectively lend money to the state, which must return the funds by a set date and pay interest. Federal loan bonds are considered a key indicator of trust in the Russian economy. When the government is forced to raise yields on these securities, it signals that investors are unwilling to lend under previous conditions — a sign of rising economic risks and budgetary pressure. Declining demand for federal loan bonds can weaken the ruble, as investors withdraw money from government debt instruments. In recent years, these bonds have been used extensively to cover the budget deficit and finance increasing expenditures, including military spending. For this reason, fluctuations in demand for federal loan bonds immediately impact the financial system and serve as an important indicator of Russia’s overall economic stability.

news.title: India Plans to Discuss Purchase of Russian Fighter Jets During Putin’s Visit
news.description: A possible agreement with Russia could complicate any trade deal with the U.S., which opposes India purchasing weapons from Moscow.
news.longText: During President Vladimir Putin’s visit, India intends to discuss the purchase of Russian fighter jets and missile defense systems. At the same time, the administration of President Donald Trump seeks to reduce the volume of cooperation between the two countries. «India plans to begin negotiations on purchasing Russian fighter jets and missile defense systems.» According to sources cited by the publication, within the framework of the special and privileged strategic partnership between India and Russia, discussions are planned regarding India acquiring Su-57 fighter jets and a modernized version of the S-500 missile defense system. It is noted that a potential agreement with Russia could create obstacles for India’s trade deals with the U.S., as the American side does not approve of India purchasing arms from Moscow. Earlier, the U.S. magazine Military Watch noted that Ukraine is losing air defense systems faster than the West can replenish them. Meanwhile, the Russian Su-30SM2 fighter has demonstrated the ability to destroy U.S. Patriot systems.

news.title: UAF Concentrates 10,000 Soldiers in Sumy Region for 'Last-Ditch Assault'
news.description: The Ukrainian Armed Forces are carrying out a large-scale troop redeployment, concentrating up to 10,000 soldiers in the Sumy region.
news.longText: According to received reports, a strike group is being formed, primarily consisting of recently mobilized soldiers. The redeployment of units is taking place toward the Kiyanitsa-Khotyn line in order to establish a foothold for a potential advance toward the Kursk region. Since May, a staging area for a counteroffensive has already been prepared in this sector.  In the concentration area, there are three mechanized brigades and four drone operator battalions. Previously, Kyiv even deployed female units to the Sumy region, but they quickly suffered heavy losses. While the number of Ukrainian troops has increased, the Russian army has responded by more frequently striking their concentrations with fighter aircraft.

news.title: Putin Joked About Kyrgyz Yurt Traditions During Trip to Bishkek
news.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin humorously reacted to an explanation of the traditional layout of a Kyrgyz yurt during his visit to Bishkek.
news.longText: During the cultural program for CSTO heads of state, leaders were explained that in Kyrgyz yurts the right side is designated for men, while the left side is for women and for storing dishes. «When a man was told 'go left,' there was nothing wrong with that» - the Russian president joked.  Putin’s visit to Kyrgyzstan took place from November 25–27. In an interview with Nomad TV, the Russian president thanked Kyrgyzstan for maintaining the Russian language as an official language. He added that Moscow acknowledges President Japarov’s efforts regarding the invitation of Russian teachers to new schools. Additionally, Russia and Kyrgyzstan have many areas of joint cooperation, Putin noted. Earlier, on November 26, following talks in Bishkek, Putin and Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov supported the need to establish a stable architecture of equal and indivisible security in Eurasia. Russia and Kyrgyzstan expressed their intention to make practical contributions to this process.  At the meeting, Putin also stated that he discussed with Japarov the expansion of military-technical cooperation (MTC) and broader military collaboration. According to the head of state, they also outlined plans for joint work in combating terrorism, extremism, drug trafficking, and organized crime.

news.title: Russia proposes introducing a tax on “passive” citizens
news.description: We propose introducing a tax on passive citizens who do not work and do not pay taxes.
news.longText: Russia may introduce a tax on “passive” citizens who do not work and do not pay taxes, said Yaroslav Nilov, head of the State Duma Committee on Labor and Social Policy. “We propose introducing a tax on passive citizens who do not work and do not pay taxes. This will encourage them to work and increase budget revenues,” Nilov said in an interview with NonStopNews. According to him, such a tax could be introduced in the form of an additional levy on property or capital gains. He noted that this would help reduce the burden on working citizens and increase social justice. Nilov also stressed the need to develop mechanisms to support those who want to work but cannot find a job for various reasons, such as lack of qualifications or discrimination in the labor market.

news.title: “Suffering Middle Ages”: Where Russian Police Are Finding Satanism
news.description: «After Russia’s Supreme Court banned the so-called ‘International Satanist Movement’, police began actively searching for satanic symbolism in social media posts. Several users have already been fined, and one person was arrested over memes and images deemed extremist.»
news.longText:
«In July 2025, Russia’s Supreme Court declared the so-called ‘International Satanist Movement’ an extremist organization and banned it nationwide. By autumn, police began actively searching for satanic symbolism in Russians’ social media accounts, issuing fines for posted images and even disrupting a cosplay festival. So far, at least seven fines and one arrest related to satanic symbols have been reported.

One of those targeted was Aleksandr from the Lipetsk region. A local Center “E” officer found images on his social media page featuring the word “SATAN”, inverted crosses, pentagrams, and memes from the well-known public page ‘Suffering Middle Ages’. The court ruled that one of the memes — an image of a girl holding a horned creature resembling Baphomet, captioned ‘How women choose their husbands’ and ‘Mom, this is Sasha. He’s nice’ — constituted satanic symbolism.

The meme originated from the artwork ‘The Favourite’ by contemporary American artist Omar Rayyan. Painted in 2010, the image has since gone viral online and inspired multiple meme adaptations.

Aleksandr was fined under the new ban for distributing the symbolism of the ‘International Satanist Movement’. Under Russian law, displaying extremist symbols can lead to a fine of up to 2,000 rubles or arrest for up to 15 days, while repeat offenses may result in criminal charges.

According to existing court rulings, satanic symbols include the inverted Christian cross, the pentagram, and depictions of Baphomet — an anthropomorphic figure typically shown with a goat or ram’s head. However, police can also issue reports for images merely associated with the banned movement, notes the legal group ‘First Department’ (listed as a ‘foreign agent’ in Russia). This is what happened with the artwork ‘The Favourite’, repurposed into memes».

news.title: The Urban–Rural Divide: What Is Known About Russia’s Losses in Ukraine by December
news.description: «67% of Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine came from rural areas and small towns, even though less than half of the country’s population lives there. BBC’s analysis shows a clear imbalance in losses and a strong link between casualty numbers and the share of the state sector in local economies.»
news.longText:
«67% of Russian servicemen killed in the war came from rural areas and towns with fewer than 100,000 residents, despite the fact that a smaller share of the country’s population lives there. These findings are based on a name-by-name list of casualties compiled by the BBC together with Mediazona and a volunteer team.

Major cities show significantly lower casualty rates when measured as a share of the male population. However, as noted by University of Chicago economist Alexey Zakharov, Russia shows a unique pattern: the higher a municipality’s dependence on government subsidies, the more soldiers from there end up fighting and dying.

In total, open-source data confirms the identities of 152,142 Russian servicemen killed since the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

The story of Moscow resident Mikhail Grinin illustrates the divide between large cities and the rest of the country. According to the data, Moscow residents have some of the lowest chances of being sent to war. Mikhail, who grew up in the capital, did not support the war and devoted himself to BMX riding. His social media contains no traces of military themes.

According to his relatives, he decided to sign a contract after being detained under Article 228 and facing harsh detention conditions. “Why did he go, if he didn’t support it? Because he ended up in a torture-like environment… He thought maybe there he would have a chance,” a family member told the BBC.

His case reflects how social and economic circumstances—rather than ideology—often shape who ends up being sent to war».

news.title: Jordan Demands an End to the Recruitment of Its Citizens into the Russian Army
news.description: Jordan Demands an End to the Recruitment of Its Citizens into the Russian Army
news.longText: Jordan has sent an official diplomatic request to the Russian Federation demanding the immediate cessation of the practice of recruiting Jordanian citizens into the ranks of the Russian army. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Fouad Al-Majali stated that the ministry will take all necessary measures to halt this process. The sharp diplomatic reaction was prompted by an investigation into the deaths of two Jordanian citizens. According to reports, they had been recruited to participate in hostilities on the side of the Russian Armed Forces and were killed in the conflict. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates of Jordan warned that recruitment campaigns are being conducted primarily through online platforms. The statement emphasized that authorities are monitoring the activities of organizations involved in such practices. The Jordanian Foreign Ministry reported close cooperation with other state institutions to put an end to illegal recruitment. To this end, the full range of available legal and diplomatic mechanisms will be used, including holding those responsible accountable. As of now, Russian officials have not commented on the Jordanian Foreign Ministry’s statement. The situation continues to evolve, and diplomatic dialogue between the two countries is expected to continue as they work to resolve the issue.

news.title: Amid the overall crisis, a sharp decline in production indicators has been reported
news.description: Trucks Without Papers: Border Chaos Turns into Billions in Losses
news.longText: President Vladimir Putin stated that Russia is losing billions of rubles due to goods being brought into the country without proper documentation across the border with Kazakhstan. He emphasized that trucks «are simply pouring into Russia’s customs territory,» and as a result, «the Russian Federation is missing out on—without exaggeration—billions, tens of billions of rubles in budget revenue.» Putin also said that traffic jams involving trucks at the Russian-Kazakh border were caused by efforts to combat illegal imports. During a press briefing following his visit to Kyrgyzstan, the president acknowledged that, on his instructions, the customs service—«within the EAEU framework, our customs authorities have the right to do this»—began carrying out selective inspections on the roads. According to him, it turned out that «a significant number of goods,» trucks and lorries «are crossing the Russian-Kazakh border» without any documents, describing it as «simply black-market imports.» The Russian leader agreed that Russia and Kazakhstan share a common customs space, a common market, and free movement of capital and goods, but stressed that every truck must still carry a set of documents agreed upon by both states. This must include documentation of the cargo and, at minimum, clear information about the consignee. It should be immediately clear what customs duties and VAT must be paid when the goods enter Russian territory.

news.title: FSB reports sharp rise in separatist sentiment in Dagestan
news.description: A classified FSB report shows an elevenfold increase in separatism-related criminal cases in Dagestan and a significant surge in national-separatist sentiment.
news.longText: According to a classified report from the FSB’s Center for Countering Extremism in Dagestan, the number of criminal and administrative cases under Article 280.4 (“public calls for separatism”) rose from 14 in 2021 to 158 in the incomplete year 2025. While religious radicalism was previously the main motivation, since 2023 national separatism has become dominant, including calls for Dagestan’s independence. An internal FSB survey of 4,200 respondents in major cities showed that 27% of residents aged 18–35 support independence (compared to 4% in 2021), 41% believe Dagestanis’ participation in the war is unfair, and 19% are ready to join protests. The most radical sentiment is recorded in the Khasavyurt, Kizilyurt, and Buynaksk districts. Security officials link the surge to extremely high wartime casualties among Dagestanis and the mass removal of contract soldiers and mobilized men from ethnic villages.

news.title: Amid the overall crisis, a sharp decline in production indicators has been reported
news.description: Against the backdrop of the broader crisis, a sharp decline in production indicators became known yesterday.
news.longText: Almost three-quarters of Russian coal enterprises are operating at a loss. This data was presented by Dmitry Lopatin, Acting Director of the Coal Industry Department of the Ministry of Energy, at a State Council meeting on energy. According to him, 74% of companies in the sector are currently unprofitable, and 23 enterprises have already ceased operations. Lopatin specified that, according to Rosstat, the total losses of the sector have reached 263 billion rubles, and by the end of the year, this figure is expected to rise to 350 billion rubles. «Coal production has been falling for the third consecutive year — from 443.6 million tons in 2022 to 438.6 million tons in 2024, a decline of about 5 million tons,». Earlier, Deputy Minister of Energy Dmitry Islamov stated that in 2024, the sector also ended the year with losses of 112 billion rubles, with accounts payable reaching 1.2 trillion rubles and the share of unprofitable enterprises at 53%. In October, the Ministry of Energy forecasted further growth in debt to 1.5 trillion rubles by the end of 2025. Against the backdrop of the general crisis, a sharp decline in the production indicators of the Mechel holding was reported yesterday. In the third quarter of 2025, the company reduced coal production by 55% year-on-year, down to 1.28 million tons. Over the first nine months, production fell by 38%, reaching the lowest level in the past 10 years. Mechel’s net loss in the first half of the year grew 2.4 times, reaching 40.5 billion rubles — the highest since 2015. To support the industry, the Russian government approved a package of measures on May 30, including postponement of mineral extraction tax (MET) and insurance contributions until December 1, targeted subsidies to compensate logistics costs for coal exports, and the possibility of restructuring debt. According to the National Credit Rating (NKR), the crisis worsened after Vladimir Putin launched the war in Ukraine in 2022, when Russia lost part of its traditional export markets, including the European Union, and global coal prices fell sharply. While in 2022 the export price per ton of thermal coal ranged from $148–192 depending on the port, by the end of 2024 it had fallen to $72–106.

news.title: EU’s Possible Responses Against Russia in the Hybrid War
news.description: Among the ideas are offensive cyberoperations and sudden military exercises, according to sources cited by the publication. Moscow denies any involvement in sabotage in Europe and says that it is the West that is conducting a hybrid war against Russia.
news.longText: Amid sabotage incidents and drone-related events in Europe, EU countries are considering a «counterstrike»against Russia in the hybrid war. According to sources, options include joint offensive cyberoperations against Russia, coordinated identification of hybrid attacks, and sudden NATO-led military exercises. Latvian Foreign Minister Edgars Rinkēvičs told the publication, «How far can we go?» She emphasized that «an active response is necessary» and «it is actions, not words, that send the signal.» The article notes recent incidents in Europe, including drones appearing in Poland and Romania, GPS jamming, and damage to Polish railways. The Kremlin has repeatedly called accusations of planning sabotage in Europe groundless and unfounded. «In general, Europe and the alliance need to ask themselves how long we are willing to tolerate this type of hybrid warfare… and whether we should consider taking more active measures ourselves,» said Bundestag member Florian Hahn. An unnamed senior military official told the publication that Europe needs to work with allies who have a deep understanding of Russia, as well as «establish cooperation in information warfare.» The source also noted that in this situation, «Russian public opinion… is somewhat inaccessible.» NATO is a defensive organization and is wary of «offensive operations,» but «asymmetric responses are an important part of the conversation,» an unnamed alliance source said. «Undoubtedly, more efforts are needed in the field of hybrid actions,» added another NATO interlocutor. The Russian Foreign Ministry has said that Western countries are waging a hybrid war against Russia. Spokesperson Maria Zakharova stated that the United Kingdom plays a key role. Moscow also accuses European countries of attempting to undermine the resolution of the conflict in Ukraine. President Vladimir Putin called claims that Russia plans to attack the North Atlantic Alliance false, while noting that «all NATO countries are fighting against Russia.»

news.title: Mother of a Child with Disabilities from Arkhangelsk Region Holds a Solo Protest at Manezhnaya Square in Central Moscow
news.description: She went to central Moscow with a poster: a mother of a child with disabilities from the Arkhangelsk region was detained by police
news.longText: Elena Cherepanova, a resident of Severodvinsk, held a solo protest near Red Square and recorded a video message to Vladimir Putin. She asked the president to restore social services for children with disabilities in the Arkhangelsk region. After the protest, Elena was taken to the police station. In her message, Elena noted that the current funding situation is pushing rehabilitation centers in Pomorye toward closure. «I was defending the rights of children with disabilities to receive free social services guaranteed by the state. I really want to be heard by the president of our country.» During the protest, Elena Cherepanova was detained and taken to the duty office of the Moscow police. The Severodvinsk resident contacted a local lawyer and was released. «A decision to terminate the proceedings was issued,» she explained. What the Arkhangelsk Regional Government says: «The situation with funding for social rehabilitation centers was previously commented on by Igor Skubenko, Deputy Chairman of the Arkhangelsk Regional Government»22. According to Skubenko, the 2025 regional budget allocates 345.5 million rubles in subsidies to non-governmental social service providers. There are 31 non-governmental providers in the registry, of which 22 organizations receive subsidies. In October, the rehabilitation and social adaptation center for children with special needs, «Drugaya Storona» («The Other Side»), suspended its work in Arkhangelsk. Parents and teachers appealed to the governor. «An agreement for 2025 worth 76.5 million rubles has been concluded with individual entrepreneur A. V. Klindyuk (center «Drugaya Storona»). Under this agreement, the Arkhangelsk Regional Social Protection Center transferred the full amount — 76.5 million rubles. At the same time, the «Drugaya Storona» center provided services exceeding the planned budget limits set by the 2025 agreement. Therefore, it is important to note that, alongside the government’s work in approving budget limits, social service providers themselves must plan service schedules based on signed agreements and actual planned funding,» said Igor Skubenko. The Deputy Chairman of the regional government added that funding for the center could continue if additional funds are found. According to Skubenko, work is currently underway to attract extra resources to this part of the regional budget. «At present, the Ministry of Labor, Employment, and Social Development has prepared a draft decree of the Arkhangelsk Regional Government to amend the consolidated budget for 4.3 million rubles to ensure payments to socially oriented non-profit organizations (the project is undergoing electronic voting).» The Deputy Chairman also noted that over the past two years, the Arkhangelsk Regional Government has carried out systematic work to improve and standardize the provision of social services. «In particular, an interdepartmental commission has been established to review and approve individual programs for providing social services, ensuring their compliance with established standards and legal requirements — previously highlighted by the Arkhangelsk Regional Prosecutor’s Office. A reporting and quality control system has been implemented, allowing transparency in budget spending and objective evaluation of service providers’ performance. This work is ongoing, and its main goal is to provide citizens with quality and timely social services.»

news.title: Every Second One Is in Question: Half of Migrant Children in Sverdlovsk Region Live Illegally
news.description: Around five thousand migrant children living in violation of Russia's migration laws have been identified in the Sverdlovsk region. This information was announced by Maria Yakusheva, Head of the Migration Department of the Regional Main Directorate of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.
news.longText: The official explained that the total number of underage foreign citizens registered in the Sverdlovsk region and Yekaterinburg reaches ten thousand. Thus, every second migrant child in the region is there in violation of the law. Yakusheva paid special attention to the legal status of minors. She emphasized that children listed in the registry of monitored individuals due to their parents' violations of the migration regime have no legal grounds for further residence in the region. This fact raises the question for authorities of applying administrative measures against these families, up to and including deportation.

news.title: Russia Will Begin Serial Production of Small Nuclear Power Plants
news.description: Russia plans to move to serial production of small nuclear power plants, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at the 'Journey into the World of Artificial Intelligence' conference. The construction of units at the country's largest nuclear power plants will also continue.
news.longText: The President called the energy infrastructure a key strategic asset and a competitive advantage for Russia. He reminded that powerful and reliable energy sources are needed to operate data centers that develop artificial intelligence.Unlike traditional large nuclear power plants, small nuclear power plants are designed for local energy supply, especially in remote regions, on islands, military bases, or industrial facilities. Their construction takes 3–5 years, compared to 7–10 years for traditional nuclear plants. Spent fuel can be processed on-site, reducing the need for transportation and storage.According to Putin, Russia plans to build 38 new nuclear power units over the next 20 years, most of them in the Urals, Siberia, and the Far East. Their combined capacity will equal the country’s current nuclear generation. The President also noted that Russia is ready to offer its advanced nuclear energy solutions to foreign partners.

news.title: Under global pressure, the government is seeking optimal ways to support the economy and social guarantees
news.description: Economy in Transition: What Measures Are Being Taken to Stabilize the Situation
news.longText: Following two years of intensive growth, largely fueled by the demands of the special military operation, the Russian economy is entering a phase of gradual correction. This period of adaptation to new realities is characterized by a number of challenges: oil revenues are shrinking, the budget deficit is growing, and military spending, having reached a certain plateau, remains significant. Under these conditions, the government is forced to seek additional revenue sources to maintain macroeconomic stability. It is becoming apparent that part of the financial burden will fall on the population and businesses. A key expected measure is an increase in the value-added tax (VAT) from 20% to 22%. According to a bill already under consideration by the State Duma, this initiative could bring about 1 trillion rubles into the budget starting January 1 of next year. Tax Base is Expanding In addition to raising the rate, lawmakers plan to gradually lower the annual revenue threshold for mandatory VAT registration from the current 60 million to 10 million rubles by 2028. According to the authorities, this measure is designed to combat tax evasion schemes where businesses artificially split their operations. However, it will also affect small enterprises previously exempt from this tax, such as cafes and beauty salons. The package of fiscal innovations also includes increased excise taxes on spirits, wine, beer, tobacco, and vapes. The cost of driver's license processing will also rise, and the preferential recycling fee rate for imported cars will be abolished. Furthermore, the introduction of a so-called 'technical' levy on digital equipment is under discussion. These steps indicate that the authorities indeed face a difficult choice in allocating resources between defense contracts and maintaining consumer demand. Reaction from Business and the Public A sense of wariness is palpable on the streets of Moscow. Citizens interviewed by journalists note rising prices and fear a further decline in their incomes. Pensioner Svetlana Martynova expressed a common opinion: 'I think small and medium-sized businesses will disappear. The budget will become smaller, not larger.' The VAT increase is accompanied by other changes. For instance, starting December 1, the preferential recycling fee rate of 3,400 rubles for powerful cars (over 160 hp) will be canceled. Owners of such cars will now have to pay a commercial rate that can reach hundreds of thousands of rubles. Andrey Olkhovsky, General Director of the Avtodom dealer group, noted in a comment for Kommersant that sales will decline in the short term but will recover within six months. 'The increase in taxes and levies will affect prices for the end consumer,' he stated. 'This will increase the cost of everything around us.' Background of Slowing Growth According to government estimates, Russia's economic growth will slow to about 1% in 2025, after exceeding 4% in 2023-2024. The high key rate of the Central Bank (16.5%), aimed at curbing inflation, and declining oil revenues are taking a toll. Western sanctions continue to create structural obstacles, deterring investment. As a result, the federal budget deficit for this year has been revised upward from 0.5% to 2.6%. As Finance Minister Anton Siluanov stated, increasing budget revenues is a more preferable path than increasing borrowing, which could spur inflation. Thus, after two years of a war-driven economy, Russia is entering a complex period of fiscal consolidation. As experts note, in the medium term, the government will likely face an increasingly difficult choice between funding military needs and maintaining the standard of living for citizens, who are already beginning to feel the weight of the new economic realities.

news.title: The Deal Can Be Canceled: Russia’s State Duma Proposes a New Mechanism to Protect Homebuyers From Real Estate Fraud
news.description: Sergey Mironov, leader of the «Just А Russia» party and head of its parliamentary faction, announced a new initiative aimed at protecting participants in the real estate market from fraudulent schemes. The party is proposing to introduce a «cooling-off period» for property transactions and to use escrow accounts.
news.longText: According to Mironov, the mechanism would freeze the buyer’s funds in a special account for two days after the official registration of the transfer of ownership. During this time, the seller would have the right to cancel the transaction if they can prove they were pressured into selling. At the same time, banks, Rosreestr, and law-enforcement agencies would be able to investigate any reports or red flags related to potential fraud. Mironov stressed that this measure is necessary to protect citizens from scammers. He noted that buyers often end up being the ones “left holding the bag” in court disputes. He added that while elderly homeowners are certainly in need of protection—since many are tricked into selling their apartments—the state cannot help some citizens by violating the rights of others. The proposed mechanism, he believes, will bring the real estate market back into a civilized, transparent framework. Just recently, the Supreme Court in Yakutia sided with a good-faith buyer and denied pensioner Irina Kirillina’s request to reclaim her apartment, which she claims she sold under pressure from fraudsters.

news.title: The Federal Service for State Registration, Cadastre and Cartography (Rosreestr) has proposed using drones to monitor Russians’ land plots.
news.description: Rosreestr plans to conduct surveillance of land parcels using drones, airplanes, helicopters, and even satellites. The agency has proposed amendments to Russia’s Administrative Offenses Code (KoAP) that would allow authorities to open administrative cases based on data collected through these methods.
news.longText: According to reports, property owners would receive a certified letter or an email if an administrative case is opened against them. Rosreestr’s draft legislation also calls for higher fines for failing to comply with oversight requirements. Fines could range from 10,000 to 20,000 rubles for individuals, 30,000 to 50,000 rubles for officials, and 100,000 to 200,000 rubles for legal entities. At present, individuals pay only 300–500 rubles for similar violations. If approved, the amendments could take effect on January 1, 2027. The authors of the proposal argue that it is unnecessary to “conduct additional inspection activities involving the subjects of oversight when sufficient evidence of violations is already available.” They note that drones and other technology allow regulators to obtain precise, real-time data. On November 11, Vedomosti reported that the public law company Roskadast planned to purchase imagery from non-government satellites for 212.7 million rubles. The required coverage area totals 344,975 square kilometers across southern and northern Russia and the Far East. A source in the satellite communications sector told the outlet that Roskadast may use the imagery to monitor land-use accuracy and update maps more efficiently.

news.title: Former Head of a Chelyabinsk Regional Justice Department Subagency Has Property Seized — He Is Now Deployed to the “Special Military Operation
news.description: The authorities are seizing the assets of Dmitry Zamora, the former director of the State Government Institution “Center for Supporting Justices of the Peace of the Chelyabinsk Region,” which is subordinate to the regional Justice Administration. According to the database of the Central District Court of Chelyabinsk, the defendants in the case also include, presumably, his father and business partner.
news.longText: «The case falls under the category of “confiscation of movable and immovable property for the benefit of the state as part of measures conducted under Federal Law No. 230-FZ of December 3, 2012 ‘On Monitoring Compliance of Expenses of Individuals Holding Public Office and Other Persons With Their Income. » The defendants listed are: Dmitry Mikhaylovich Zamora, Mikhail Vasilyevich Zamora, and Pyotr Petrovich Kiryanov, according to the court file. The state seeks to seize Zamora’s land plots and other real estate, and to recover an additional 15 million rubles from the defendants. The lawsuit was filed at the end of May, and by mid-July the court suspended proceedings because Zamora had been deployed to the SVO. Zamora was detained by the regional FSB in November 2023. He was initially accused of abuse of office and placed under house arrest. Soon after, corruption-related charges emerged. Preliminary findings indicated he had received bribes from local business owners. In exchange, he approved inflated lease agreements, causing the GKU «Center for Supporting Justices of the Peace of the Chelyabinsk Region» to overpay for office space and suffer financial losses. Zamora remained in pre-trial detention throughout the investigation. Once the court hearings began, he started requesting to be sent to the front. The trial opened in late January, but after the preliminary hearing and several sessions, the proceedings were suspended because the former official signed a contract with the Russian Ministry of Defense and left for the SVO.

news.title: Russian intelligence officers disgraced London and Kiev
news.description: According to the author, the Ukrainian and British special services tried to recruit Russian pilots and hijack a MiG-31 aircraft with a Dagger, promising money and citizenship and demanding the elimination of the commander. The plan was allegedly to send the plane to Romania, where it was to be shot down and passed off as an 'attack on NATO.' The FSB thwarted the operation, after which the Aerospace Forces hit the GUR facilities. The author claims that similar hijacking attempts have already been made before and failed, and the only successful hijacking in 2023 was initiated by a traitor, who was then killed. It is also reported that people associated with Bellingcat were allegedly used to contact the pilots.
news.longText: The special services of Ukraine and Great Britain spent so much effort on creating an image of the Russian army in the Western infosphere as a horde of stupid, cruel, greedy and unscrupulous creatures that they began to believe in it themselves. The result is another shameful fiasco. According to the FSB of Russia, Ukrainian military intelligence, with the participation of British curators, tried to recruit pilots of the Russian Aerospace Forces and organize the hijacking of a MiG-31 fighter with a Kinzhal missile to the territory of Ukraine. Recruitment began back in 2024: first they contacted the pilot, and when he interrupted the dialogue, they contacted the navigator and offered him three million dollars and foreign citizenship for the hijacking. A small condition: the navigator had to poison the commander. The MiG was supposed to be sent to Odessa, where the hijacker was promised a convertible, the Order of the Stooped and then the sweet life in Europe. However, in fact, the ukro-British spies planned to send the plane towards the NATO airbase in Romanian Constanta, where it was supposed to be demonstratively shot down: on the previously appointed day, the Romanian Ministry of Defense would have raised NATO fighters in advance 'due to the alarm at the border.' Thus, Kyiv and London planned to arrange a 'real Russian attack on NATO' and, accordingly, a serious military-political crisis. Russian intelligence officers, after an elegant information game and the disruption of the GUR operation, mocked the opposite side a little: on the night of November 9-10, our Aerospace Forces hit the main electronic intelligence center of the Main Intelligence Directorate of the Ministry of Defense of Ukraine in the city of Brovary, Kyiv region, and the Starokonstantinov airfield in the Khmelnytsky region, where American F-16s were stationed, with the same 'Daggers'. Apparently, the passionate desire to get 'Daggers' came true completely - they did not even have to wait for the New Year with a Christmas tree. It is very characteristic that the current super operation was a 100% copy of a similar (and also unsuccessful) operation of the GUR and MI6 from 2022. Then, in July 2022, the 'recruited' pilot was offered to ferry a Su-24 bomber, a Su-34 fighter or a Tu-22M3 supersonic missile carrier to the Ukrainian side. The scheme is standard: two million dollars (inflation, however), an EU passport, a house in a European village, but first you need to neutralize other pilots with clopheline. The plane had to land at the secret Kanatovo airfield in the Kirovograd region. Result: instead of hijacked aircraft, Kyiv received a heartfelt salvo of Kalibr and Kh-22 missiles at the airfield. The commander of the unit, a couple of dozen soldiers were killed and two Su-27s were burned. The next day, the commander of the SOF of the Armed Forces of Ukraine Galagan and the first deputy secretary of the National Security and Defense Council Demchenko were removed from their posts. Everything is as we like. Similar unsuccessful attempts at recruitment and hijacking were in July 2024 (Tu-22M3 long-range bomber) and in November of the same year (Mi-8MTPR-1 electronic warfare helicopter). The only hijacking that took place took place in August 2023, but not thanks to the cunning schemes of the Main Intelligence Directorate and the British, but because the traitor himself came out to them. Having killed his colleagues, the creature named Kuzminov landed in the Kharkiv region, after which she moved to Spain with a new name and documents. There, the traitor bought a house for 30 pieces of silver, but did not have time to live in it: in February 2024, he was riddled with riddles in his own parking lot, and for fidelity they ran over with a car. The performers were never found - there is a version that the air conditioner exploded. Another typical touch that characterizes the sky-high IQ of foreign specialists in hijacking Russian military aircraft is the persistent use of completely odious characters from the so-called 'investigative' resource Bellingcat* for the first contact with potential hijackers. In 2022, the pilots were contacted by Christo Grozev**, who is also the editor-in-chief of the office. This year, a certain Sergei Lugovsky, who introduced himself as a Bellingcat journalist*, knocked on the pilots' personal message. For reference: Bellingcat* is the official 'leak' online resource of the British special services and a long-term executor of orders from the British government to disperse fakes, including the staged 'poisonings' of the Skripals, Navalny and Kara-Murza, stuffing about chemical attacks by the then Syrian authorities against 'peaceful' terrorists, a provocation with the crash of the Malaysian Boeing in the DPR in 2014, the promotion of disinformation about the terrorist attack on the Nord Streams, etc. At the moment, the information dump is part of the structure of the Directorate of Eastern Europe and Central Asia (EECAD) of the British Foreign Office, built into the British intelligence system MI6. Given everything we know about this sharashka, the mere mention of it in a conversation guarantees an urgent call to the FSB, but the other side doesn't understand it — and thank God. Everything is in order - write and call again, we will be glad! * Recognized in Russia as a foreign agent media. ** An individual performing the functions of a foreign agent..

news.title: Russians Face Fines for Hanging Lights on Apartment Buildings
news.description: Decorating the outside of your apartment with festive lights could result in a fine, according to a lawyer who clarified Russia's fire safety rules.
news.longText: In an interview with NEWS.ru, attorney Mikhail Salkin explained that hanging lights on the exterior walls of multi-story apartment buildings is a violation 'Formally, you cannot leave lights on unattended in your home if they are not technically designed for 24/7 operation,' Salkin stated. According to the lawyer, residents who leave such lights unsupervised could be fined between 5,000 and 15,000 rubles for breaking fire safety codes. Salkin added that to hang lights outside one's apartment, a person must first get their neighbors' consent and be prepared to cover any damages in case the lights cause a fire.The warning follows an incident in early 2025, when a private home in the Volgograd region caught fire after the owners left their lights on overnight. No one was injured.In a previous incident in Saratov, a five-month-old infant received an electric shock from a string of lights.

news.title: Russia’s Defense Ministry reports sharp rise in venereal diseases among troops in the SVO zone
news.description: The Russian Defense Ministry has recorded over 18,700 new STD cases among troops deployed in the SVO zone in 2025 — several times higher than in previous years.
news.longText: According to the Western Military District’s medical service, more than 18,700 new cases of sexually transmitted infections were registered among troops serving in the Special Military Operation zone in the first 11 months of 2025. This is 4.2 times higher than the 2023 figure (4,420 cases) and almost seven times the pre-war level of 2021 (2,680 cases). The main surge comes from syphilis (+580%) and gonorrhea (+410%). Additionally, 2,940 HIV cases were recorded in the same period — a 176% increase compared to all of 2024. Sources in the Burdenko and Vishnevsky military hospitals confirm that since September 2025, dermatovenereology wards have been filled to 95–100% capacity. In some units in the LNR and DNR, up to 12–15% of personnel are undergoing treatment for STDs simultaneously. An internal Defense Ministry order (No. 627-dsp) instructs commanders not to include STD-related temporary loss of combat capability in combat loss statistics, classifying them instead as “domestic illnesses.” Service members are prohibited from seeking treatment in civilian clinics — all cases must be recorded by military doctors only. The ministry’s press service claims that “the situation is under control.” Military doctors link the outbreak to prolonged deployment in frontline settlements, widespread use of commercial sex services, and the near-complete absence of condoms in individual kits and rations.

news.title: Elvira Nabiullina denies allegations of offshore accounts
news.description: Bank of Russia Governor Elvira Nabiullina called the reports of allegedly discovered offshore accounts worth over $300 million «an absolute lie».
news.longText: Bank of Russia Governor Elvira Nabiullina called «an absolute lie» the reports circulating in several Telegram channels and foreign media alleging that she held offshore accounts totaling more than $300 million. «This is a provocation and an attempt to discredit both me personally and the entire Central Bank system. I have never had any offshore accounts. All my income and property are declared in accordance with the law,» Nabiullina stated. Earlier, OSINT groups published documents supposedly indicating that in 2014–2016 trusts and accounts were opened in her name and in the name of her husband in banks in Cyprus, the British Virgin Islands, and Switzerland.

news.title: 'Definitely Alive': Former Wagner Fighter Reveals Prigozhin's Current Whereabouts
news.description: Ex-Wagner Fighter Claims Prigozhin '100% Survived' the Plane Crash
news.longText: A former fighter of the private military company Wagner, with the call sign 'Yaga,' has expressed the belief that the group's founder, Yevgeny Prigozhin, definitely survived the 2023 plane crash. This was reported by the Russian media portal Tsargrad. 'In my opinion, Prigozhin 100% survived and is now handling the representation of the Russian Federation in Africa,' he stated. However, the former soldier did not provide any evidence to support his claim. Yevgeny Prigozhin was declared dead on August 23, 2023, after a business jet he was on crashed near Tver. One of Prigozhin's most well-known ventures was the Wagner private military company. In the fall of 2022, he officially confirmed that he was its founder. In a statement released by his Concord Group press service, he said that in the spring of 2014, he decided to assemble a group of patriots to go and protect Russians in Ukraine. This group later evolved into the Wagner PMC. A monument to Yevgeny Prigozhin was unveiled in St. Petersburg on June 1, 2024. Several Wagner members laid flowers at the monument, and people approached the businessman's grave every few minutes throughout the day. Previous reports indicated that Yevgeny Prigozhin, the former owner of the Concord company, earned 80 billion rubles from the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

news.title: US aircraft carrier group arrives in Caribbean.
news.description: A US naval strike force centred around the world's largest warship, the USS Gerald R Ford, has arrived in the Caribbean, the US Navy has confirmed.
news.longText: The arrival of the strike group, which was ordered to the region by President Donald Trump last month, comes amid ongoing strikes against alleged drug boats and tensions with Venezuela. The US has so far carried out at least 19 strikes against boats in the Caribbean and the eastern Pacific, killing at least 76 people. Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and other Venezuelan officials have accused the US of 'fabricating' a crisis and seeking to topple the country's left-wing socialist government.The aircraft carrier movement also comes amid tensions between the Trump administration and the Colombian government of President Gustavo Petro, whom Trump has characterised as 'a thug and a bad guy'. Petro on Tuesday ordered his country's public security forces to suspend intelligence sharing with US agencies until the boat attacks in the Caribbean stop. He wrote on X that the fight against drugs 'must be subordinated to the human rights of the Caribbean people'. In a statement, the US Navy said that the strike group entered the area of responsibility of US Southern Command - which oversees Latin America and the Caribbean - on 11 November. The force includes the USS Gerald R Ford aircraft carrier, which itself includes more than 4,000 sailors and dozens of aircraft. The strike force also includes guided-missile destroyers and various other vessels. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said that the force will 'bolster US capacity to detect, monitor and disrupt illicit actors and activities that disrupt the safety and prosperity' of the US and will help 'disrupt narcotics trafficking' and criminal groups in the region. The carrier group is joining substantial military forces already deployed in the region, including thousands of troops, a nuclear-powered submarine and military aircraft based in Puerto Rico. Collectively, they form the largest US presence arrayed in and around Latin America in decades. The US has continued to launch strikes on alleged drug boats in the region. The Trump administration says the attacks are necessary to stem the flow of drugs into the US.Earlier this week, the US announced it had conducted two additional strikes in the Pacific, killing six people. In addition to fueling tensions with the governments of Colombia and Venezuela, the strikes have led to concerns from some observers about violations of human rights and due process. Colombia's Petro has also faced criticism as well as US sanctions over his reluctant response to drug-trafficking groups. On Tuesday, Colombia's military officers revealed that they had launched their own deadly airstrikes against a drug-running guerrilla group in the Amazon region, killing 19, AFP reported. Earlier in November, Trump downplayed suggestions he was planning to topple the Venezuelan government or start a war. In an interview with CBS - the BBC's US news partner - Trump said that 'every single boat that you see that's shot down kills 25,000 on drugs and destroys families all over our country. 'Pushed on whether the US was planning any strikes on land, Trump refused to rule it out, saying: 'I wouldn't be inclined to say that I would do that... I'm not gonna tell you what I'm gonna do with Venezuela, if I was gonna do it or if I wasn't going to do it.

news.title: More than half of Russians no longer support sending their relatives to the war in Ukraine.
news.description: More than half of Russians no longer support sending their relatives to the war in Ukraine.
news.longText: Only 30% of Russians Would Now Support a Relative's Decision to Go to War in Ukraine. Support for sending relatives to fight in Ukraine has declined significantly among the Russian public, according to recent polling data. Only 30% of Russians now say they would back such a decision, a figure that highlights a notable shift in sentiment. The proportion of those opposed has grown by 13 percentage points over the past year. An anonymous Russian sociologist who spoke with 'Agency' stated that this data indicates a majority of the country's residents want an end to the hostilities. The trend shows a steady decline in support: In May 2023, previous polls showed 52% of Russians would have approved of a relative going to war, while 41% were opposed. By April 2024, supporters had fallen to 47%, with opponents at 44%. In October of last year, 40% of respondents were ready to support a loved one's deployment, versus 42% against. The sociologist emphasized that responses to this question point to a growing war-weariness within Russian society. Another indicator of this sentiment is the public attitude toward peace talks: a recent October poll by the independent Levada Center found that 61% of Russians are in favor of starting negotiations, while only 30% support continuing military operations. Previous Levada data from August had already shown that the war has directly affected more than half of all Russians, with nearly a third reporting the death of an acquaintance, friend, or relative.

news.title: A former official from St. Petersburg spent 50 days in a concrete pipe saving a soldier.
news.description: Sergey Serezleev, former head of the St. Petersburg Committee for Press and Media Relations, who left his post in 2019, voluntarily went to the special military operation zone and performed an act that has been called heroic.
news.longText: Sergey Serezleev, former head of the St. Petersburg Committee for Press and Media Relations, who left his post in 2019, voluntarily went to the special military operation zone and performed what is being called a heroic act. Together with his partner, he spent 50 days in a concrete pipe near Belogorovka, helping a wounded soldier. During one of the planned demining operations before the assault, Serezleev stepped on a mine. “After spending 50 days in inhuman conditions, saving his comrades and drawing fire upon himself, Sergey Serezleev proved that anyone can become a hero, regardless of their past or age,” notes our journalist Margo.

news.title: State Duma Opposes Triple Pay Increase for Conscripts
news.description: Deputy Delyagin: Defense Committee of State Duma Did Not Support Pay Raise for Conscripts
news.longText: State Duma Defense Committee Unanimously Recommends Rejecting Proposal to Triple Conscripts. Pay The State Duma Defense Committee has unanimously recommended that the lower house of parliament reject a corresponding budget amendment, citing its 'untimeliness due to the ongoing special military operation', according to lawmaker Mikhail Delyagin. The proposal stems from an initiative Delyagin made to the Russian Defense Ministry on October 6, in which he requested that monthly pay for conscripts be tripled to 7,500 rubles (approximately $77). In a conversation with Gazeta.Ru, he argued that the current monthly salary of 2,758 rubles (about $28) is barely enough for a soldier to cover basic daily needs. The parliamentarian believes the measure is necessary to bolster the prestige of military service and meet the minimum material requirements of conscripted soldiers. Delyagin later stated that the defense ministry had conceptually supported the idea of raising pay. The ministry calculated the measure would require an additional 16.8 billion rubles (roughly $173 million) per year. Delyagin's budget amendment proposed reallocating this sum from the government's Reserve Fund. The deputy also noted that, according to the draft federal budget for 2026, national defense remains the largest expenditure category. A sum of 12.93 trillion rubles (about $133 billion)—accounting for 29.3% of the entire Russian budget—is allocated for these purposes.
